title: The Ringers' Rule
author: the pilgrims' ringers, before the Stair was cut
body:
# For whoever has the rope

*Punched in tin, and the tin gone the colour of the heath.*

---

Ring once for a sail seen.

Ring twice for a sail near.

Ring three times when they are ashore, so the ones on board who are still at sea know that the ones who went first are standing on something.

Do not ring for a sail you only hope for. The bell carries over the Hush and it carries a long way and it does not come back.

*Scratched under it, later, with a knife:* The last ship was the *Sa Oune*, out of the Isles, forty-one aboard. Rung three times. Stair cut the year after. Nobody needs the bell now.

*Under that, newer again, and wet when you found it:* one.

title: Vaelost: the top course, as far as it can be read
author: a Sayer of the Circle, unsigned
body:
# Vaelost, the kept one

*A field-book page. The hand is neat until it is not.*

---

From the foot, the glass at full draw, the sun low behind me (the only light it can be read by): the name runs round the top course, cut deep, Oroth letters, and the course is turned so that it can be read from the Choir and from nowhere else.

First sign: *VA*. Certain.

Second: *EL*, or *ETH*. The weather has had it.

Third and fourth: gone into the glass where the stair ran up and turned. The glass has grown over them.

Last: *-OST*, which is how the tower got its name from us, and which is not a name, it is an ending. The Builders put endings on things they meant to keep.

---

The Order will pay to know whose name it is. The Order will not say what it will do with the answer. I have measured the course three evenings and I have decided that I do not want to be the one who tells them.

*In the margin:* Somebody has been climbing it. There are hand-marks in the ash on the glass stair, going up, and none coming down.

title: Two lines on a slate
author: two pilgrims, a child and somebody older
body:
# What the back bench heard

*Chalk, a child's letters, large:*

MAM WHISPERD AT THE FRONT AND I HEARD IT HERE LIKE SHOUTING. SHE SAID DONT BE FRIGHTEND. I WAS NOT UNTIL SHE SHOUTED IT

---

*Scratched under it with a pin, small, a grown hand:*

We went on south in the morning. The Order says a whisper in this hall is heard at the back and a shout is heard on the heath. I did not shout. I want it written somewhere that I did not shout.

title: The Row-Book of the Bell Garden
author: the knights of the ring who stand the rows
body:
# Rows, and what hums

*The Order's square hand, several knights, one after another.*

---

Fourteen rows. Nine bells a row but the sixth, which has eight and a hole. Every bell a different note; nobody has found two alike and three of us have tried.

When the Toll hums the whole garden hums with it, a half-note under. We go and stand in the rows until it stops, one knight to a row, because a bell with somebody standing by it hums lower, and nobody knows why, and it is the only thing we can do.

---

The Toll hummed on the third night of the thaw. I stood the fourth row. The tenth bell hummed a whole note under the others and went on after they had stopped. I stood by it till dawn. It stopped at dawn.

I have written it down. I have not told anyone. I have put this book under the tenth bell so that whoever stands the fourth row next knows which one it is, and can decide for themselves whether to tell.

*Under, another hand:* It did it again. I told Cadwen. Cadwen said count it.

title: Which mouth sang
author: a knight of the Order, counting
body:
# The Row of Mouths, at dusk

*Count-paper. A pillar's number and a night, and nothing else, for a long time.*

---

31. 9. 44. 2. 17. 58. 9. 23. 40. 6. 51. 14. 33.

9 twice. Nothing else twice.

---

There are sixty mouths in the row. A single note from one of them every dusk, a different one each night; the pilgrims walk the row with their mouths shut, which is the only custom on the heath older than the Order, and I have started to think I know why.

If you walk the numbers on the ground, pillar to pillar, the way the singing went, you walk towards the Choir and away from it and towards it again, like somebody pacing.

The ninth mouth is the one nearest the Choir.

title: The fountain, counted
author: the knight who empties the fountain, spring 1043
body:
# The fountain, spring

*The Order's square hand.*

---

Emptied at first light as every spring. Carried to the chapter-house in four baskets as every spring. Counted on the long table with the Vigil Book open, as every spring.

Pilgrims walked down since last spring, by the Greywatch readings: two hundred and six.

Bells in the fountain: two hundred and seven.

---

Counted again. Two hundred and seven.

The extra bell is small and old, a child's size, and its clapper is not tied, and there is no name round its lip at all. It is the only bell in the fountain that is warm.

Cadwen says the count is the count. I have put it back in the fountain. I do not know that that was right. I have put this in with it so that somebody knows what I did.

title: What the sea brought in
author: the scavengers of the Driftwood Camp, in turns
body:
# The strand, by the tide

*Several hands, some of them barely letters.*

---

Planks, eleven. A cask, empty, Tollmere mark. A boot. A gull, dead.

Planks, four. A net-float of green glass, Salt Isles make, the first in nine years. We have hung it up.

Nothing, three tides running. Went to the Grey Wreck for her ribs.

A barge. Tollmere. Sealed. Crew gone. Wat's man said leave the seal, and we have left it, and we are not proud of it.

---

*A newer hand, careful:* A boat went by at dawn under the strand, rowing north, two in her, Salt Isles rig. Did not come in. Waved. We waved back. First Salt Isles boat on this water in forty years and she waved at us.

title: The Dig at the Thirteenth: the third season
author: the Sayers' camp at the Thirteenth
body:
# The Thirteenth, season three

*A dig-book: finds, levels, arguments, in at least three hands.*

---

Trench C down to the shoulder seam. The neck is whole. The head is whole. The head is not the head of the twelve: the twelve have (had) the Choir's faces, all alike. This one has a face of its own. G. M. will not say whose. W. A. says it is obvious and will not say either.

---

The choristers came again at dark and stood round the trench and held the note at the head until dawn. Nothing broke. The spoil heap was warm in the morning.

---

Found in the fill over the mouth: a pilgrim's hand-bell, clapper untied, the lip worn smooth where a name would be. Pilgrims do not come here. It is under three feet of ash that has not been disturbed since the Ash Winter.

---

*G. M.'s hand, pressed hard:* It walked away from the ring. I am more certain of that each season. It walked away and it lay down here, face in the ash, and it has been waiting a thousand years for somebody to dig it out and ask it why.

title: Buried in the west quarter
author: the Order's burial knights, many years
body:
# The Unrung Graves

*A name, a year, the words 'bell kept, clapper to the chapter-house'. Over and over, in the Order's square hand.*

---

Joss Wendle, of Merrowby, 971. Bell kept, clapper to the chapter-house.

A woman of the Vale, no name given, 988. Bell kept, clapper to the chapter-house.

Ivo Brand, 1002, a child. Bell kept, clapper to the chapter-house. His mother walked on alone.

*Thirty more names, the same words.*

---

The count of posts in the quarter is one more than the count of names on this list. Nobody on this list is missing. The extra post has a bell on it with its clapper taken out, like the others, and a name round the lip, and the name is on no list the Order keeps.

We have not dug to see if anybody is under it. The Vigil Book says do not make a fuss.

title: A year's bells, scored through
author: Eddery Wray
body:
# 1043, the count

*Tallies in fives, row under row, then a line through all of it.*

---

Four hundred and six on the first night of the thaw. Four hundred and nine. Four hundred and six. The Toll hummed: a half, by the Order's rule, which I never held with. Four hundred and twelve.

The Choir has four hundred and twelve bells, if you count the chapter-bell at the Ash, which the Order does.

Four hundred and thirteen, on the night after the hum.

---

I have scored it through. A count one more than there are bells is not a count, it is a mistake, and I have made it every night since, the same mistake, which is not what a mistake does.

I will start again tomorrow. I have started again every tomorrow for nineteen years.

title: The Gauge Book
author: the Surveyors of the Circle at the Gauge, 1011-1043
body:
# How far the grey has come

*Readings, one line a year, in the Circle's copperplate. The gauge's divisions are in Oroth measure, which the Circle keeps for exactly this.*

---

1011. Grey edge at the fortieth division. Gauge set up. Surveyor Ansfrid Wenlow.

1012. Forty-one. 1013. Forty-one and a half. 1014. Forty-two.

*Thirty years of lines, never going back. The hands change twice.*

1042. Sixty-three. Surveyor Idrin Fenn.

1043. Fifty-eight.

1043, second reading. Fifty-eight.

1043, third reading, at dusk, in case it is the light. Fifty-eight.

---

*Fenn's hand, smaller:* I have not sent this year's line to the Spire. The Circle files what it is sent. If I send this, somebody will have to believe it.

title: What the Tallymen pay, this month
author: Coll Brisket, the Scavengers' Ring
body:
# PRICES

*Chalk. Crossings-out. More crossings-out.*

---

BRONZE, BUILDERS', CLEAN: 4 a pound. ~~5~~

BRONZE, FUSED: 1 a pound, and only if they're in a good mood.

GLASS, BLACK, FROM THE BED: 2 a hand. Sayers pay 3. Sayers do not come back for more.

BELLS: WE DO NOT SELL BELLS. THE ORDER BUYS THEM BACK AT WHAT WE PAID AND THANKS US AND WE FEEL LIKE DIRT. LEAVE THEM.

ANYTHING WITH WRITING ON: the Circle. Do not read it first. Nell.

---

*Under it, fresher:* NO DIGGING WEST OF THE RING TILL I SAY. — C.

title: Four names cut in the Last Milestone
author: the four who came back up the Stair, Y.T. 867
body:
# Four names, cut on the way back

*Cut into the back of the last of the Builders' milestones, low down, where you would only see them sitting against it. Four hands, four knives, one of them a pilgrim's eating-knife by the width of the cut.*

---

AVELINE

ODO

MERRIT

SALLOW

---

*Under the four, one line, in the first hand:*

We came back up. We will not stand at the ring with the ones who stayed. We will keep our own count, where we can see the road we came back up, so that if any of the twenty-six come back after us there is a fire.

title: The counts on the Ninth Waystone
author: two hands, the Order's and another
body:
# The Ninth Waystone, the side towards the Choir

*Scratched into the stone, a year a line, the Order's bell-counts for the year's first night.*

---

1019: 404. 1020: 406. 1021: 405. 1022: 406. 1023: 407. 1024: 406.

*Then nineteen years of nothing. The stone there is smooth, and pilgrims have sat on it.*

1043: 413.

---

The last line is in a hand the Order does not know: long strokes, pressed hard, the fours made open at the top the way they were taught at the Novices' Seats before Cadwen's time. Under it, very small, a mark like a seat seen from behind, turned round.

title: The count on the Tenth Waystone
author: an unknown hand
body:
# The Tenth Waystone, under the coin-bowl

*Scratched under the lip of the bowl, where only somebody putting a coin in would see it.*

---

413. 413. 413. 414.

*And an arrow, cut with care, pointing off the road west across the open heath, towards nothing a pilgrim would walk to.*

title: The Weighhouse's scales
author: the Builders; read by a Sayer's rule
body:
# The pans

*What the scales say, read by the Circle's rule: a weight is a word in Oroth, and a pan down is the word said.*

---

For a hundred years the east pan has been down, fused, and the Sayers read the word cut on its rim as *vael*, kept, held.

The west pan is down now. The east is up, clean, as if nothing had ever been in it. The word cut on the west pan's rim has been under ash for a thousand years, and it is *hesk*: silence, the Hush.

---

If the Builders weighed something here and found it wanting, the Order says, it was the note. The pan has moved. Either the note is lighter or the Hush is heavier. The Surveyor at the Gauge would like it measured. The scales cannot be moved to measure them. That is the whole difficulty.

title: The Greyline stones, as the Wardens set them
author: the Wardens of the Hearth, one stone a Naming Day
body:
# The Greyline

*Cut into the tops of the stones: a year, and the Warden who set it.*

---

1031, Hobb. 1032, Ada. 1033, Ada. 1034, Roswith. *And on, each stone a pace or two behind the last, going back towards the Vale, for twelve years.*

1042, Tam Hurdlegate.

1043, Tam Hurdlegate. *This stone stands a long stride in front of 1042's, on the grey side, in ash. The ash round its foot is thinner than the ash round 1042's, and there is grass in it, green at the root.*

title: The Last Order at Turnback
author: the chapter-master of Turnback, Y.T. 974
body:
# To whoever keeps Turnback after us

*The Order's square hand, the ink gone brown. Nailed inside a sarcophagus lid in the undercroft, face in, as if hidden from somebody who could still read.*

---

We are going to the Ash. All of us who are still ourselves.

Aveline kept this house sixty years and died in the gate-arch counting, and we laid her in the undercroft with her mace and the Count, and in the spring she came up the stair and took the Count back off the lectern and went on with it from the night she died.

Three of the knights have gone down to her since. None of them came back up the stair ourselves.

We are leaving the Count. We cannot take it off her and we will not fight her for it. She is keeping it better than we are.

If you are reading this, and you are one of the twenty-six, there is a fire in the gate. Sit by it. She will count you.

title: The Diggers' Last Tally
author: Nell Brisket, scavenger
body:
# Down the new shaft

*Charcoal on a scavenger's tally-board, the letters getting bigger as the lamp got lower.*

---

Three of us down. Jory's rope. Coll said wait. We did not wait.

Roof sound. Floor sound. Halls. Benches all facing one way. Nobody in them.

Somebody singing. Not in a hall. Under us.

Tam went to see. Tam came back and sat down on a bench facing the way the benches face and would not get up.

It is not unkind. That is the worst of it. It is TEACHING.

I am going down to get Tam. If this board comes up without me tell Coll to fill the shaft.
